title: Scale Composer: interactive fleet scaling controls with change playback and throughput inspector
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build an interactive "Scale Composer" in Console that lets operators create, preview, and replay fleet scaling actions (manual, schedule, and autoscale adjustments) while correlating those actions against observed throughput, latency, and cost. The Composer should combine: 1) an editable timeline of scale events (what changed, when, who), 2) a throughput inspector that overlays token/sec and tail latency per model variant, and 3) a change playback UI to simulate historical outcomes with optional 'what-if' edits before committing.

Why: Customers buying Dedicated want predictable throughput guarantees and confidence when applying scaling/override changes. Current console pages are fragmented across dashboards, audit logs, and one-off presets — operators ask for a single surface to understand cause/effect, preview changes, and safely roll forward or rollback.

Non-goals: Not replacing low-level autoscaler engine logic; not exposing undocumented internal scaling heuristics. This is an operator surface built on top of existing autoscale policies and audit events.

Success criteria / Acceptance criteria:
- Users can create, edit, and save scale events (increase/decrease capacity by N GPUs, set concurrency cap, pin model variant) in a timeline draft without applying.
- Timeline shows user, timestamp, reason, playback markers, and linked GitHub PR or runbook.
- Throughput inspector overlays historical token/sec, 95th/99th tail latency, and per-route cost delta aligned to the timeline.
- Playback mode can simulate applying a draft timeline against historical traffic (30d window) and produce estimated SLO/latency and cost deltas. Estimates should use existing cost model (batching & quantization knobs) with +/- ranges.
- Change history is auditable and supports rollback to any prior committed state; rollbacks create new timeline events, not destructive edits.
- RBAC respects Dedicated account roles; only fleet-operator and admin roles can commit changes; viewers can preview/playback.
- Instrumentation: events emitted for compose_start, compose_commit, compose_simulate, compose_rollback with sufficient metadata for experiments and billing signals.

Design/UX notes:
- Main canvas: left column = editable timeline (stacked events), center = throughput inspector chart with overlay of model-variant and per-route series, right column = change details and 'what-if' knobs.
- Compact list and full-expanded timeline modes. Inline diff view for autoscale policy edits.
- Keyboard shortcuts for playback (space = play/pause, J/K = step back/step forward).

Telemetry/implementation constraints:
- Use existing telemetry buckets for throughput (route_token_rate) and latency (route_p95, route_p99). If gaps exist, add lightweight sampling with feature flag.
- Simulation will run in a sandbox that replays real metrics and feeds them to the cost/latency estimator in the backend; accuracy expectation: +/- 10% for cost, +/- 20% for tail-latency in extreme surge cases. Communicate confidence intervals in the UI.

Rollout plan:
1) Alpha: internal operators + 3 enterprise customers (feature-flagged). Collect qualitative feedback and instrument simulation accuracy.
2) Beta: expand to all Dedicated customers with role gating; add exportable playback reports.
3) GA: enable in Console by default, link to runbook templates and API to apply composed timelines via infra playbook.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- How to represent multi-region fleets during playback? (Option A: aggregate across regions; Option B: split timeline by region). Preferring split-by-region in alpha for clarity but aggregated default for compact view.
- Simulation performance vs accuracy: running full replay for 30d may be slow; propose sampling + extrapolation for >7d windows.
- Cost model debt: need to surface model assumptions and let users override batch/quantization knobs in simulation.

Acceptance sign-offs required: PM, ENG (runtime & infra), Design, Security (if KMS or logs exposure changes), and Customer Success for pilot picks.
